summary.text: A 69-year-old man with COVID-19 diagnosed by PCR was hospitalized on 27 March 2020 for uncontrolled fever of one week. Chest radiography showed right lower lung field infiltration. He received lopinavir/ritonavir, hydroxychloroquine, ceftazidime and convalescent plasma therapy; oxygen requirements and fever improved for 3 days after the plasma infusion before the condition deteriorated.

Because of respiratory distress and gas exchange deterioration he was mechanically ventilated on hospital day 9, and VV-ECMO was started on hospital day 13 for increased oxygen requirements. Ultra-protective ventilation was used; antibiotics were changed to colistin and meropenem and dexamethasone was given during VV-ECMO. Table 2 records a tracheostomy and an inflow line in the right femoral vein.

After 11 days of VV-ECMO (hospital day 24), chest radiography findings and lung compliance showed signs of recovery, and VV-ECMO was discontinued after 14 days. He successfully recovered from COVID-19-induced ARDS; Table 2 reports no bleeding or superinfection, survival on ECMO, weaning, ICU and hospital survival, and a hospital stay of 65 days.

summary.text: A 56-year-old woman with COVID-19, hospitalized for a week elsewhere, was transferred on 7 June 2020 for worsening respiratory distress after mechanical ventilation was applied just before transfer. On arrival chest radiography showed extensive bilateral infiltration; ventilation at maximum settings with a neuromuscular block left percutaneous oxygen saturation at approximately 50%.

VV-ECMO was applied immediately on hospital day 1 with cefotaxime, convalescent plasma therapy and dexamethasone, with ultra-protective ventilation. Pupillary light reflex was checked three times daily; on day 7 the response was reduced, sedatives and the neuromuscular blocker were stopped, spontaneous respiration recovered, and both were given again after a mental status check.

Chest radiography and lung compliance began to improve on hospital day 18 and VV-ECMO was discontinued on hospital day 21. She recovered from COVID-19-induced ARDS; Table 2 reports no bleeding or superinfection, survival on ECMO, weaning, ICU and hospital survival, and a hospital stay of 61 days.

On hospital day 6 mechanical ventilation was applied for respiratory distress, hypoxemia and hypercapnia, but hypoxemic and hypercapnic respiratory failure worsened.

VV-ECMO was implemented on hospital day 11, with ultra-protective ventilation; meropenem, levofloxacin, convalescent plasma therapy and dexamethasone were given during VV-ECMO. Chest radiography and lung compliance began to improve on hospital day 33 and VV-ECMO was discontinued on hospital day 38.
